anomalies.observed: The anodes of D1, D3 and D42 all sit on /NET0129 and nothing else. That net has no supply connection, so the three status LEDs have no path to +3V3. Their cathodes are driven through R78, R56 and R77 from the CM4 Ethernet and activity LED nets.
anomalies.expected: Status LED anodes should be tied to a supply rail, as with the other indicator LEDs in the design (e.g. D24 anode on +3V3, D36 anode via R32 to +3V3), so the LEDs can be driven active-low from the CM4 pins.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet and activity indicator LEDs D1, D3 and D42 cannot conduct, so these status indications never light.

anomalies.observed: D20 pin 4 (A2 anode) and R76 pin 2 both sit on NET0036, which is also driven by U8 pin 4 (Y). R76 runs from the K2 cathode (Net-(D20-K2)) back to that same node. The second LED channel is therefore in a loop with its own driver output and cannot be driven.
anomalies.expected: Following the pattern of the other indicator LEDs (anode on a driver node such as NET0086, cathode through a series resistor to the opposite driver or GND), the K2 resistor should return to a different node from the anode drive.
anomalies.impact: The K2 channel of the dual LED D20 cannot be lit, and the CAN-connector pin 6 (J11/J33) is also tied to this LED drive node.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows status LEDs with anodes on an isolated, unpowered net (D1, D3, D42) and a dual-LED channel that loops back onto its own driver node (D20 channel 2). Both look like wiring errors, though the spec does not cover LED wiring, so confidence is moderate.
